SETTLED IN THIS PASS, 2026-10-12. The front matter used to say the part letters are 'too degraded to read even at 500 ppi', and that blanket claim contradicted the rest of the record: the small italic letters inside the plate really are smudges (figures/p226-fig141-part-letter-zoom.png, sha256 7cbdc30475362e51a0259156752016b1a33ef57746464bf4c7385d2c9d64294f), but at the right edge of the large globe there is a letter, while the text layer of the same page renders the sentence describing this very bulb as 'In Fig. 141 the bulb comprises an incandescent lamp globe Z, in the neck of which is sealed a barometer tube &, the end of which is blown out to form a small sphere s'. A record that contradicts itself is the one case section 6.6 allows a figure to be re-opened for, so it was re-opened at 500 ppi in this pass (the crops below were copied out of gitignored books/tmp/f06figrec/, this task's working directory) and the label is an italic L. Two reads settle it, both against the print of the same page, and figures/README.md records the exact box of each. (a) The printed line that names this globe: the text layer puts the word it renders 'Z,' at x 245.088-252.351 pt, y 384.330-392.338 pt of a 267.264 x 464.544 pt page, so 6.9444 px per pt in the 500 ppi render, and cropping that box (x 1381, y 2645 to x 1770, y 2743) shows the line ending '...lamp globe L,' - a serif bar across the top of the letter, one stem slanting down-left, a foot running right and turning up at its end, then a comma. That is an L; a Z needs a top bar the full width of the letter and a flat bottom bar, and this glyph has neither. The crop is figures/p226-textline-globe-L.png (1167 x 294 at 3x, sha256 c2d99d772a24d88a4da080d1f087babc6ebbbd0518eaf6fbd69431f242fd7fe3). (b) The plate label is the same letterform: mapped at native pixels with no interpolation, the glyph at x 795-818, y 1467-1490 of the render has the same three strokes in the same arrangement as that printed italic L - short serif bar above the top of the stem, one stem slanting down-left, foot running right and turning up. It is 23 px tall against the body text's 33 px, which is why a 4x LANCZOS upscale of it reads as a '7': the interpolation smears the serif bar into a top bar and the rising foot into a flat one, and a blurred L looks like a 7. Those two crops are figures/p226-fig141-globe-label.png (180 x 160 px, box x 740 to 920 and y 1440 to 1600 of books/tmp/scan-p244-500ppi.png, sha256 f8f427dd67fcebbacb0717808dfc5ad3beaeb9787be459b353dcb9e04619cfa0) and the same crop at 4x, figures/p226-fig141-globe-label-4x.png (720 x 640, sha256 b8c69c9b293e1a164a0aa6897b71f76e13294886f72f4923490bea083a108e6e); the read was made from the native pixels, not from the upscale. The text layer is wrong twice over in that one sentence - it gives the globe as Z where the type says L, and the barometer tube's label as '&'. The clean body text agrees with the plate: 'When the globe L (Figs. 141 and 142)' on printed p. 227, and the p. 228 sentence the page quotes verbatim in its FAQ answer, 'it is usually sufficient to grasp the globe L with the hand'. What did NOT change, and why: the alt still names shapes rather than part letters, because the letters that would have to be named inside the plate are the ones that genuinely are illegible, which is what section 6.6 asks for in that case; the caption and the quoted description still elide the letter positions, because check_quotes.py checks quotes against the OCR text and a quote corrected to 'globe L' would fail the tool that guards the quotes. The label is recorded in the front matter and in figures/README.md, not in the page copy. The front-matter sentence is now narrowed to the letters that actually are illegible, which is what this contradiction asked for; the other two figures were not re-opened, because section 6.6 re-opens only a figure whose evidence is missing or contradicted and theirs is neither.
